name: Juvederm Voluma
lead: Juvéderm Voluma (marketed in the US as Juvéderm Voluma XC) is a cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal filler made by Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company. It is a 20 mg/mL gel built with the company's Vycross cross-linking technology and, in the XC version, contains 0.3% lidocaine. [1] It is designed for deep injection to restore or add volume, and is best known as a cheek and midface filler.

According to Grokipedia, the US FDA approved it for midface volume deficit in 2013, for chin augmentation in 2020 and for temple hollowing in 2024. [1] In looksmaxxing and aesthetics discussions it is commonly described as a high-lift filler for cheekbones and chin projection; it is a non-surgical, temporary, reversible alternative to implants and osteotomies.

Controlled and open-label studies have followed midface treatment for up to 24 months and report volume improvement and high patient satisfaction. [2][3] Reported adverse events include injection-site reactions and, less commonly, delayed-onset nodules; filler complications in general have also included vascular events. [4][5][6]

paras: Voluma is a sterile, biodegradable, viscoelastic gel of HA produced by bacterial fermentation and cross-linked with the agent BDDE using Vycross technology. [1] Laboratory comparisons of filler rheology classify cross-linked HA gels by their stiffness (elasticity), viscosity and cohesivity, and describe Voluma among the firmer, higher-lift HA products used for deeper tissue planes. [7][8][9]

Labelled uses in the US are cheek augmentation to correct age-related midface volume deficit, chin augmentation and, since 2024, temple hollowing, in adults over 21. [1] Registered trials have also examined other sites, including the nose, hands/feet pads and HIV-associated facial lipoatrophy; these are investigational. [10][11][12]

A retrospective chart review of delayed-onset nodules after Voluma injection over 68 months documented this complication and its management. [5] A later retrospective review of delayed adverse events in 4,500 patients treated with a smooth cohesive 20 mg/mL HA filler also examined the frequency of delayed reactions. [6]

An analysis of US FDA adverse-event reports and litigation concluded that fillers carry risks including vascular compromise and that these feature in lawsuits. [4] Product labelling lists contraindications including severe allergies, a history of anaphylaxis and allergy to lidocaine or gram-positive bacterial proteins. [1]

A 24-month study of an HA filler for midface volume deficiency reported effectiveness and acceptable safety over that period. [2] A multicenter, single-blind randomized controlled study reported patient-reported outcomes at two years for midface treatment. [3] A retrospective analysis of 102 cases earlier described the volumizing effect of the product. [13] A randomized split-face histology study compared a calcium hydroxylapatite filler with an HA filler. [14]
Registered trials include chin augmentation (n=221), temple hollowing, an Asian-nose study (n=29), and a comparison of a competing gel with Voluma XC for midface volume (recruiting). [10][15][16]

timeline.event: US FDA approval for midface volume deficit (per Grokipedia). [1]
US approval extended to chin augmentation. [1]
US approval extended to temple hollowing. [1]

lore.intro: Voluma is discussed in looksmaxxing communities as a way to simulate higher cheekbones or a stronger chin before, or instead of, surgery. Forum posters compare it with surgical options.

claims.claim: Cheek and chin filler can approximate the effect of implants without surgery
claims.believers: Proponents describe filler as a lower-commitment way to test a change in projection before considering surgery.
claims.experts: Clinical studies report volume improvement and satisfaction for midface and chin treatment, with results that are temporary and require repeat treatment. [2][3]

claims.claim: Fillers are safe because they can be dissolved
claims.believers: Users cite reversibility with hyaluronidase as a safety net.
claims.experts: Laboratory studies have tested how HA fillers respond to hyaluronidase; adverse-event and litigation reviews document vascular and other complications. [4][17]

card.summary: Firm hyaluronic acid cheek and chin filler from Allergan; temporary volume with studies behind it, plus filler-class risks.
card.note: Filler complications can include vascular events; results are temporary.

quick.overview:
Voluma is a hyaluronic acid gel injected deep in the face to add volume, mainly in the cheeks, and later approved in the US for chin and temples.

Studies follow treated midface patients for up to two years and report improvement and satisfaction; the effect is temporary and reversible with hyaluronidase.
quick.mechanism: A cross-linked HA gel (Vycross) is placed deep, near bone, where it adds volume and lift to overlying tissue and slowly degrades over months.
quick.risks: Reported effects include swelling, bruising, delayed nodules and, rarely, vascular complications. It is a prescription medical device administered by licensed professionals.
